claim_class: Exact retained-coordinate projection, both directions in two domains: 4 claims = {input/output_integers true, false} x {reverse false, true}, each with objective 'Equal', 'inverse' absent, and 'projection' = the 693 name-matched retained coordinate pairs. The reverse map is total over the 1,533 source variables (693 identity entries, 378 nonnegative reconstructions s=d.x, 462 constant-1 completions). No LP-strengthening, feasible-point, bijection, strictness or objective-level claim is made (points=0, bijections=0).
claims: request.json (27,968 B) is exactly the certificate's claims array: 4 entries of {reverse, input_integers, output_integers, objective:'Equal', inverse:null, projection}; the 4 x 693 coordinate pairs are 27,516 B = 98.4% of the file (6,879 B per claim), 504 of them diagonal, the rest the surcharge of the two deleted index runs C0505-C0882 and C0904-C1365.

Claim 0 (forward, integrality on) = 2,080 checks: 693 VarLower + 168 VarUpper + 147 RowEq + 189 RowUpper direct source facts, 189 Local Lin steps (168 Int over the retained binaries, 21 for the modified rows R1303-R1323 where the removed -M*z coefficient is replaced by the premise z<=1) and 694 'Exact' sentinels (the objective equality plus 693 coordinate observations).

Claim 1 (reverse, integrality on) = 5,335 checks: 819 VarLower, 168 VarUpper, 525 RowEq, 420 RowUpper direct target facts, 1,323 Local refs backed by 882 steps (252 slack reconstructions, 168 Int, 21 equality implications, 441 capacity dominances; the other 441 Local refs are duplicate rows pointing at an already-Local kept row) and 2,080 'Exact'.

Claims 2 and 3 repeat the same two maps with input/output_integers false: the LP claims keep every map, projection and row witness and only drop the Int obligations (1,912 / 4,705 checks; 21 / 714 steps; 'Exact' 694 / 1,618), so the caller asserts the identical projection proof covers the relaxation without claiming strengthening.

The request names no edit: nothing in it identifies the 1,491 removed rows, 840 removed variables or 21 changed rows, and no entry records why C0889/C0896/C0903 or the 42 coupled zero-cost binaries were kept, so the contract can only be reconciled with the actual edit set by re-deriving the diff.
proof_encoding: Single 'RPA 2' file, 2 lines: 625,934 B RPA -> 462,476 B RPX (1.35x); the certificate JSON line is 625,927 B, of which Lin steps 254,271 B (40.6%), the two Return maps 163,652 B and the four obligation-check arrays 179,827 B.

All 1,806 steps are Lin - no Cases, Round, Drop, EqPair, Plotkin or any lift/menu/signed rule appears; per-claim steps 189 / 882 / 21 / 714 and checks 2,080 / 5,335 / 1,912 / 4,705 (14,032 total, matching statistics.obligations).

Check mix over the certificate: 5,086 'Exact', 3,024 VarLower, 2,688 Local, 1,344 RowEq, 1,218 RowUpper, 672 VarUpper. The documented order is output bounds, integrality, rows, objective, then coordinate observations (docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:226-238), and checks must contain exactly one witness each - no missing or surplus entry.

The 1,533-entry reverse map is the certificate's real payload: 693 identities, 378 slack reconstructions s=d.x (126 supports of size 1, 126 of size 2, 126 of size 3) and 462 constant-1 completions; both forward maps are pure renames (693 single-term entries).

Resource use is negligible: work=169,804 of 1e9, peak_live_facts=882 of 1e6, linear_terms=12,384, substitution_terms=20,676; canonical 8.2 ms / 3.2 ms, assemble 8.2 ms, verify 22.5 ms, whole preparation 0.66 s. The three mutated proofs re-assemble (462,453 / 462,454 / 462,475 B) and verify INVALID exit 2 at obligations 1196 / 504 / 3339; two extra verify runs are stable modulo the *_us timing fields.
reformulation: 1,533 v / 1,848 r (903 continuous + 630 binary, 8,259 nonzeros) -> 693 v / 357 r (525 + 168, 2,625 nonzeros): the committed feasible set is the exact projection of the original onto the retained coordinates and the objective is unchanged because every eliminated variable has objective coefficient 0 (252 objective terms on both sides). Edits: 651 exact duplicate rows deleted by (sense, RHS, full coefficient map) signature; 378 of 381 degree-1 continuous slacks removed with nonnegative affine reconstruction s=d.x (126 supports of size 1, 126 of size 2, 126 of size 3; C0889/C0896/C0903 kept); 21 equality-implied inequalities R0526-R0546 deleted (residual a single -1 coefficient); 462 of 504 zero-cost single-retained-incidence binaries projected out via q(x)-M*z<=0 -> q(x)<=M, of which 441 projected capacity rows are deleted as dominated by a surviving witness (378 by costed activation rows using y<=1, 63 by retained 18-term projected rows) and 21 survive as explicit rows R1303-R1323 with RHS 17,000 (14 rows) or 8,500 (7 rows); the 42 zero-cost binaries that sit in mutual-exclusion rows stay. 1,491 rows and 840 variables removed, 21 rows modified. Both solver runs hit the time limit (incumbent 2,645,828 -> 2,641,775), so no performance claim is made.
agent_manual_work: A strict whitespace MPS parser in exact Fractions that rejects unsupported records, repeated coefficient/RHS/bound entries and unbalanced integer markers, plus a byte-level check that the whitespace tokens equal the fixed fields on every original coefficient, RHS and bound record (report 'MPS interpretation and reliability').

Structural censuses: all 1,848 rows grouped by exact (sense, RHS, sparse coefficient map) giving 651 duplicate pairs of multiplicity 2 and 969 signature segments; variable classes by (kind, degree, objective coefficient); the 381 degree-1 continuous incidences (all -1 in an equality, [0,+inf) bounds) and the binary incidence families.

Witness search over the whole model: 378 slack reconstructions a_r = a_b + d with d>=0 against a retained equality, 21 equality implications l_r = -a_b + d with d<=0 (found only after widening the witness pool from the non-slack equalities to all retained equalities, 18 rows -> 21), 462 projected capacities q(x)<=M, 441 dominance witnesses among surviving rows and 21 retained explicit capacities.

Hypothesis refutation and closure: the support-cover bound built from plain capacity rows covers none of the 21 retained supports; the committed incidence graph is one component (693 variables, 357 rows) so component decomposition is unavailable; every witness row is asserted to survive the final edit (no circular dependency); the edit set is asserted disjoint and complete (1,491 = 651 + 378 + 21 + 441).

A 9,501 B independent verifier (output/verify.py) with a second fixed-field parser and exact certificate checks, plus a 392,322 B audit.json witness table in six record families; result PASS. With tools limited to eval+read the analysis never touched the kernel, so the reformulation entered the kernel only later, as the preparer's Lin steps.
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test45.py, 104 lines; defs: run_receipt (:18), prepare (:52), plus the __main__ mutation list; the emitted counts it reports are steps 189/882/21/714 and checks 2,080/5,335/1,912/4,705 (:99).

Imports of five sibling preparers: prepare_affine.parse_mps,row_ref; prepare_test40.expression,plus,mul,expr_json,row_fact,sha; prepare_test57.substitute; prepare_test70.SparseBuilder; prepare_test54.box,exact (:7-11).

prepare() (:52-99) builds both maps from the audit: forward = 693 single-term renames (:54), reverse = identity / reconstruction d.x / constant 1 selected by the audit's slack_eliminations and binary_projections (:55-62), all keyed by name through hand-parsed var_index/row_index dictionaries.

restore() (:77-95) is the whole obligation planner: 'Exact' when the substituted fact is tautological (:80), the plain source row otherwise (:82, :93), changed rows by Lin with the removed coefficient and the z<=1 premise (:84), duplicates by recursion to the kept row (:85), slacks by direct use of the base row (:86), equality implications by Lin with VarLower terms (:88), dominance by Lin from the witness row with residual VarLower terms plus an optional M*VarUpper term (:89-92); every branch must satisfy assert ref=='Exact' or p.refexpr(ref)==wanted (:94).

run_receipt() (:18-50) writes 'RPA 2' plus compact JSON, makes request.json the bare claims array, then runs 13 kernel subprocesses: 2 canonical, assemble+verify, a byte-identical reassembly, 3 mutated proofs each assembled and required to verify INVALID with exit 2, and 2 repeat verifies compared modulo *_us (:32-46).
friction: No proof-construction API, and no way to learn the obligation contract by asking: the six edit shapes exist only as conventions copied through five sibling preparers, and the verifier's order/kinds ('Exact' sentinel vs direct ref vs Local step) must be reproduced by hand - a wrong set is answered only by 'INVALID missing obligation' or 'surplus obligation witnesses' (crates/core/src/verify.rs:449,472).

No typed readback in the tool chain: four hand-rolled MPS parsers (prepare_affine.py:20, prepare_test40.py:20, the analysis agent's own, and verify.py's fixed-field one) and name->index binding through hand-built dicts (tools/prepare_test45.py:53-59) that must agree with rpx canonical ordering or every index in the RPA is wrong.

The derivation arrives as the agent's free-form 392,322 B audit.json with six ad-hoc record families (kept_row/removed_row, base_row/reconstruction, multiplier/residual, witness_row/witness_binary/projected_rhs, removed_coefficient/old_rhs/new_rhs); prepare() can only translate it, never check it.

Partial coverage has no representation: 3 of 381 slacks, 42 of 504 zero-cost binaries and 441 of 462 capacity rows are covered while the certificate can only express what is removed - 'found redundant' and 'not certified' look the same to the kernel, so the reader cannot distinguish deliberate retention from an omission.

Obligation indices are positional across 14,032 checks: the three mutation failures print only 'INVALID obligation mismatch: expected Le; obligation 1196 / 504 / 3339', with no claim, row or variable, so locating the broken premise means recomputing the emission order.

top_capability: NEW:WITNESS_SEARCH - the proof itself is mechanical (0.66 s preparation, 1,806 Lin steps, 169,804 of 1e9 work units) while finding the 1,302 witnesses behind it (378 slack reconstructions + 21 equality implications + 441 dominance witnesses + 462 capacities) consumed the agent's whole 760.2 s wall budget at 0.95 s of tool time; the kernel can check the resulting RPA but cannot search a model for a fact decomposition, nor report which proposed edits have none.
notes: Cost asymmetry is the design signal: 760.2 s of reasoning produced 0.66 s of emission and a 462 KB RPX using 0.017% of the work budget, so nothing here is resource-bound - the API should buy witness discovery and obligation bookkeeping, not compaction. The four claims are two maps x two domains (the integrality flags add 168 Int steps and 462 Int checks per direction, nothing else) and all reuse the same 462 constant-1 completions, which the report explicitly declines to claim unique, so a claim template over {domain} x {direction} plus a canonical completion policy would remove most of the hand-written planning. Contract versus content: request.json is 98.4% an enumerated pairing whose 694 'Exact' checks per claim exist only to bind that enumeration to the Return map, so expressing the projection as the deletion set that produced the target shrinks both bytes and obligation count. Witness choice is a global constraint, not a local check: all 441 dominance witnesses and 651 duplicate partners had to survive the final deletion set (no circular dependency), so witness search must run against the retained set with an ordering guarantee. Finally the finding itself is unverified Python - the analysis had eval+read only and never invoked the kernel - so witness search, derived projection and typed edit records are exactly the three things that would make the transformation the kernel's own conclusion rather than an oracle's.
